subject: Re: ApexPay RFP — preservation, on-demand extracts, and chain-of-custody
messages:
From: Trevor King <trevor.king@apexpay.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: audrey.lin <audrey.lin@apexpay.com>, apextapay-security <apexpay-security@apexpay.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: ApexPay RFP — logging & export questions

Sofia — thanks again for taking ApexPay's logging and retention questionnaire. Attached is a short list of follow-ups from our compliance team. The primary asks we need clarified for the RFP evaluation are: 

1) Preservation windows: our regulators require at least 7 years for transaction-related audit trails but we want to understand what Redwood keeps in hot vs cold storage and how quickly we can retrieve a full forensic bundle.

2) On-demand extracts: do you provide per-request NDJSON/Parquet exports? Can we request exports scoped by account, timeframe, and artifact type (audit-events, request/response payloads, model versioning metadata)?

3) Tamper evidence / chain-of-custody: we need a summary of how you guarantee the integrity of exported artifacts (hashing, signed manifests, timestamping, and whether we can bring our own KMS for signing).

4) SLA & delivery: example timelines for exports >100GB, delivery channels (S3 push, signed download, scp), and who is responsible for egress costs in Dedicated vs Private deployments.

Please reply with a concise description and any sample playbooks or a link to your export runbook. I've attached the short questionnaire — appreciate a response by 11/20 so we can keep the RFP timeline.

Thanks,

Trevor King
Head of Compliance Programs
ApexPay

Attachment: APEX_RFP_Logging_Questions.pdf (1 page)
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Trevor King <trevor.king@apexpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ApexPay RFP — logging & export questions

Trevor — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise response addressing each of your numbered items; I also attached a short \"preservation + on-demand extract\" playbook (redwood_preservation-extract-playbook.pdf) with examples and sample manifest formats. If helpful we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week.

1) Preservation windows and storage tiers
- Hot window: default 90 days of high-fidelity audit records and request/response payloads stored on low-latency object storage (SSD-backed hot tier).
- Nearline: next 11 months (months 3–12) retained on optimized nearline storage with retrieval SLA of 24 hours for full-bundle requests.
- Cold/archival: after 12 months we move immutable snapshots to cold archive for up to 7 years (configurable per account / contract). Cold snapshots are retained as signed bundles and metadata indices.
- Legal hold: we support indefinite legal hold on specific accounts/top-level resources — items under legal hold do not expire and are kept as immutable, versioned snapshots.

2) On-demand extracts
- Formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Parquet (columnar), and gzipped tarballs of JSON for payload bundles. Each extract includes a manifest with SHA-256 hashes for every object and a signed manifest file.
- Scoping: extracts can be scoped by tenant/account, user-id, resource-id, model-version, and arbitrary time ranges. Multiple artifact types can be included in the same bundle (audit-events, request/response payloads, config/rollout metadata, model binary fingerprints).
- Filtering: server-side filters support predicate pushdown (e.g., event_type IN (auth, config_change) AND request.user_id = '...').

3) Tamper evidence & chain-of-custody
- Hashing and manifests: every exported bundle includes a machine-readable manifest (NDJSON) with per-file SHA-256 and a top-level manifest hash.
- Signing: manifests are signed using Redwood signing keys; for Dedicated and Private customers we support BYOK (bring-your-own-KMS) where manifests can be signed with a customer-managed key (AWS KMS or HSM).
- Timestamps & notarization: export timestamps are RFC3339 UTC; for high-assurance exports we can produce a notarized timestamp using a third-party time-stamping authority on request (add-on).
- Audit trail: export operations themselves are logged as immutable audit events (who requested, which filters, which manifest hash) and are available for downstream ingestion by your SIEM/forensics team.

4) SLA & delivery options
- Delivery channels: S3 PUT to a customer-owned bucket (recommended for large exports), HTTPS signed download (suitable for up to ~100GB), or secure transfer (scp/rsync) to a pre-authorized host.
- Throughput & examples: small extracts (<100GB) are typically delivered within 24–48 hours; larger bundles (100GB–1TB) are delivered within 3–7 business days, subject to scheduling and region-specific egress capacity. For Dedicated deployments we provision transfer nodes to meet contracted windows.
- Egress & costs: for Hosted/Shared customers egress costs are billed per our standard pricing; for Dedicated and Private deployments we can contract to include egress in the reserved capacity fee or pass-through to the customer depending on the agreement.

Playbook & attachments: see attached PDF for sample manifest formats, recommended query predicates for scoped extracts, and a checklist your security team can use for QA.

If ApexPay needs a stronger guarantee (e.g., same-day retrieval SLA for 1TB forensic bundles), we can surface a tailored Dedicated plan and a transfer runbook — I'll loop in Rishi (cc) for sizing and exact timelines.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: ApexPay RFP — preservation, on-demand extracts, and chain-of-custody

Sofia/Rishi — thanks for the thorough write-up, that's exactly the level of detail the review board wanted. A couple quick clarifications before we close this section of the RFP: 

- For BYOK signing, does Redwood support multi-tenant keys (one KMS per account) or only a single signing key per deployment? Our preference is per-tenant signing keys.
- Can you confirm manifest hash uses SHA-256 only, and whether you include a PGP-signed copy as well?
- For the 24-hour nearline retrieval SLA, is that from request creation or from approval (we have a staged approval workflow that sometimes adds 4–6 hours)?

If you can answer those 3 bullets inline we'll mark the item complete. Also, we may ask for a sample signed manifest (redacted) to verify the format.

Trevor
